items.video_title: How To Inspection A Car | How To Inspect a Used Car For Purchasing or Car Investment & Earn Money
items.video_description:
How to inspect a used car before buying? In this video, we’ll walk you through a basic level car inspection checklist – perfect for beginners! Learn how to check the body frame, Car Paint, engine, gearbox, suspension, AC performance, tyres, and interior condition without needing a mechanic.
This is your first step to becoming confident in buying and maintaining your own car. Whether you're buying your first car or investing in a used vehicle, this video will help you avoid costly mistakes.

*In Shaa Allah, I’ll also bring you an advanced inspection guide in the next video so you can become a pro at car inspection.*

*✅ Point 1: Body Frame & Alignment*
• *Check the car from the side* – look for any uneven surfaces, dents, or wave-like patterns. These may indicate bodywork after an accident.
• *Inspect the body frame closely* – if there are irregular gaps between the bonnet, fenders, or doors, it might be a sign of a previous accident or poor realignment after repairs.
________________________________________
✅ *Point 2: Paint Condition & Body Seals*
• *Visually check for uneven paint texture* – known as "orange peel" or patchy surfaces. It’s a clear sign of repainting.
• Use a *paint thickness gauge* to check for inconsistencies. A variation in readings often means the car has been repainted. Green status shows its original paint.
________________________________________
✅ *Point 3: Front Support (Patti) Check*
• Look for *hammer marks or uneven surfaces* on the front support panel (patti).
• *Loose or opened bolts* on the front suggest that the area has been worked on – this usually happens after a front-end accident.
• *Factory bolts should be tight* and have original paint marks intact.
________________________________________
✅ *Point 4: Engine Condition*
• Open the *engine oil cap* – if you see thick, black deposits (sludge), it means the engine wasn't maintained properly.
• Use a flashlight or your phone camera to check for *leaks or oil stains* in the engine bay
________________________________________
✅ *Point 5: Transmission / Gearbox*
• Start the car and *shift gears while idle. * There should be no jerks, delays, or noises.
• For *manual cars, * the clutch should feel smooth and not too hard.
• For *automatic cars, * gear shifts should be smooth without any lag or hard jerks – delays or clunks are warning signs.
________________________________________
✅ *Point 6: Suspension Check*
• With the car stationary, *turn the steering wheel fully left and right in motion circles * – listen for any *"click"* or *"thuk thuk"* sounds, which indicate suspension or steering rack issues.
• Take a *test drive over uneven roads* – listen for knocking sounds or vibrations, which may point to worn-out suspension components.
________________________________________
✅ *Point 7: Car Interior (Cabin Inspection) *
• Check the *wear on the steering wheel, gear knob, and handbrake lever* – excessive wear with low odometer reading may mean the meter has been tampered with.
• Inspect the *roof lining* – roughness or sagging usually appears in high-mileage or poorly maintained cars.
• Look in the *trunk/spare wheel area* – if the floor is scratched or worn, the car might have been used as a taxi or not maintained well. A clean and shiny trunk often indicates a well-kept vehicle.
________________________________________
✅ *Point 8: AC Performance*
• Use a *car AC temperature meter* (available in the market) to check how much the temperature drops.
• Turn on the AC – it should start cooling quickly. The *compressor sound should be smooth* with no rattling or whining noises.
________________________________________
✅ *Point 9: Tyres Condition*
• Insert a *1 rupee coin into the tyre tread* – if the tread doesn't cover the coin markings, the tyres are worn out.
• Find the *manufacturing year on the tyre sidewall* – old tyres (over 5-7 years) lose grip and can be dangerous, even if the tread looks okay.

Worn Out Tappet Cover Packing Results In Engine Oil Leakage 

We had this 2012 Toyota Corolla Altis visit one of our MotoFyx car repair workshop for an annual service. Intending to use the car for a long distance journey, the car owner wanted to have the car thoroughly inspected and hence reached out to us for assistance.

Upon a detailed inspection of the car by our expert technicians, while performing the annual service, there was visible leakage of engine oil which was observed from under the hood & also the spark plugs electrodes were in bad condition due there was engine misfiring issue. Upon further diagnosis the source of engine oil leakage was observed to be from the tappet cover packing, which had worn out overtime and was in need of immediate replacement.

*Function of tappet cover packing: 
- The tappet cover packing is a protective rubber material designed to properly seal the cylinder. The tappet cover packing prevents any oil or fuel from leaking out of the engine, as it travels around the camshafts rockers and valves 

*Symptoms of a worn out tappet cover packing: 
- Buring oil smell
- Valve cover is dirty and leaking oil 
- Engine is low on oil level
- Check engine light on cluster 

*Solution: 
- The valve cover was dismantled 
- Faulty tappet cover packing was removed and the tappet cover was cleaned 
- Cam shaft and valve rockers were cleaned 
- New Toyota genuine tappet cover packing was installed onto the tappet cover and anabond was applied 
- Tappet cover was then installed back onto the engine head 
- Spark Plugs Were Replaced 
- New engine oil was filled and annual service was performed
